stages.title: PART IV: CONSTITUTIONAL DIRECTION WITHOUT DIRECT ENFORCEMENT
sequence: Governance duty guides law and policy

groups.heading: CONSTITUTIONAL BASIS
items: Part IV contains Articles 36-51.
Article 36 imports the Part III meaning of State.
Article 37 denies direct court enforcement.

groups.heading: OPERATING FORCE
items: The principles remain fundamental in governance.
The State must apply them in making laws.
Law, budgets and administration translate direction into outcomes.

groups.heading: CHECK / LIMIT
items: Non-justiciable does not mean optional.
A directive alone does not create an automatic writ remedy.
Courts interpret and review; they do not continuously design welfare budgets.

stages.answer_line: Part IV directs the same State restrained by Fundamental Rights toward welfare goals, linking limited government with social transformation.

stages.title: ARTICLES 38-43B: WELFARE AND DEMOCRATIC ECONOMY

groups.heading: JUSTICE AND DISTRIBUTION
items: Article 38: justice-informed social order and reduced inequalities.
Article 39(a)-(f): livelihood, resources, concentration, pay, labour and children.
Article 39A: equal justice and free legal aid.

groups.heading: SELF-GOVERNMENT AND SECURITY
items: Article 40: village panchayats.
Article 41: work, education and assistance within economic capacity.
Articles 42-43: humane work, maternity relief and living wage.

groups.heading: PARTICIPATION AND CO-OPERATION
items: Article 43A: workers in management.
Article 43B: voluntary, autonomous, democratic and professional co-operatives.
Exact text controls classification and implementation examples.

stages.answer_line: Articles 38 to 43B convert the Constitution's welfare commitment into linked directives on distributive justice, access to justice, local self-government, labour dignity, social security and democratic economic organisation.

stages.title: ARTICLES 44-51: REFORM, CAPABILITY, ECOLOGY AND PEACE
matrix: four limbs; no automatic treaty incorporation

groups.heading: CIVIL REFORM / CAPABILITY
items: Article 44: Uniform Civil Code endeavour.
Article 45: care and education until age six.
Article 46: weaker sections, especially SCs and STs.

groups.heading: HEALTH / PRODUCTION / ECOLOGY
items: Article 47: nutrition, living standard, public health and prohibition.
Article 48: scientific agriculture and animal husbandry with cattle protection.
Article 48A: environment, forests and wildlife.

groups.heading: HERITAGE / RULE OF LAW / WORLD ORDER
items: Article 49: nationally important monuments and objects.
Article 50: judiciary separated from executive.
Article 51(a)-(d): peace, relations, international law and arbitration.

stages.answer_line: Article 49 is not a generic culture clause; it protects nationally important monuments, places and objects within the Parliamentary-law framework.

stages.title: CLASSIFICATION AND AMENDMENTS: TEXT REMAINS CONTROLLING

groups.heading: ANALYTICAL GROUPS
items: Socialistic: justice, labour and welfare.
Gandhian: village, cottage/co-operative economy and uplift.
Liberal-intellectual: reform, environment, heritage, judiciary and peace.

groups.heading: OVERLAPS / CAUTION
items: Articles 43, 46, 47 and 48 overlap.
The Constitution does not name the three categories.
Always answer from exact Article text first.

groups.heading: AMENDMENT OVERLAY
items: 42nd: 39(f) recast; 39A, 43A and 48A inserted.
44th: Article 38(2).
86th: Article 21A and recast Article 45.
97th: Article 43B.

stages.answer_line: The socialistic, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual grouping aids revision, but overlapping provisions show that it is scholarly classification rather than constitutional text.

stages.title: FR-DPSP EVOLUTION: CONFLICT TO BASIC-STRUCTURE HARMONY

groups.heading: EARLY CONFLICT
items: Champakam Dorairajan (1951): enforceable rights prevail over conflicting directives.
Amendments responded through protective and redistributive devices.
I.C. Golaknath (1967) restricted amendment of Fundamental Rights.

groups.heading: AMENDMENT POWER AND LIMIT
items: 24th Amendment affirmed constituent power.
25th Amendment created Article 31C for Article 39(b)/(c).
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) allowed amendment but protected basic structure.

groups.heading: HARMONY DOCTRINE
items: 42nd Amendment attempted to extend Article 31C to every DPSP.
Minerva Mills (1980) invalidated that extension.
Harmony between Parts III and IV forms basic structure.

stages.answer_line: Parliament may amend rights and legislate to implement Part IV, but the basic structure - including judicial review and harmony between Parts III and IV - limits that power.

stages.title: ARTICLE 31C: NARROW SHIELD AND REVIEWABLE NEXUS

groups.heading: ENTRY CONDITIONS
items: The law must genuinely further Article 39(b) or 39(c).
Article 39(b) concerns resources serving the common good.
Article 39(c) prevents harmful concentration.

groups.heading: LEGAL EFFECT
items: The surviving shield operates against Articles 14 and 19.
A statutory declaration is not conclusive by itself.
Courts test the law-object nexus and constitutional limits.

groups.heading: CURRENT CONTROL
items: Property Owners Association (2024) confirms the surviving first limb.
Not every private asset is automatically a community resource.
Basic-structure and judicial review remain.

stages.answer_line: Article 31C protects laws genuinely implementing Article 39(b) or (c) from Articles 14 and 19 challenges, but basic-structure review prevents unlimited insulation.

stages.title: IMPLEMENTATION AND ARTICLE 39A: ACCESS TO JUSTICE

groups.heading: IMPLEMENTATION CHAIN
items: Directive -> competent law -> budget -> rules, institutions and delivery.
Courts review legality and use DPSP in rights-consistent interpretation.
Audit, legislatures and elections assess performance.

groups.heading: LEGAL-SERVICES ARCHITECTURE
items: NALSA -> State -> District -> Taluk legal-services bodies.
Section 12 provides category and income routes.
Section 13 requires prima-facie satisfaction of the case.

groups.heading: LOK ADALAT CONTROL
items: Ordinary Lok Adalat settles by consent and cannot decide merits after failure.
Permanent Lok Adalat handles public utility disputes before litigation.
Bounded merits power follows failed conciliation, subject to statute.

stages.mechanism_strip: Official NALSA access and Suhas Chakma (2024) connect statutory architecture to monitored prison legal-aid delivery.
stages.answer_line: A Directive Principle becomes credible through a competent law, funded institutions, accountable delivery and measurable outcomes—not enactment alone.

stages.title: ARTICLE 44 AND EVALUATION: REFORM WITHOUT FALSE BINARY

groups.heading: CONSTITUTIONAL CASE
items: Uniform civil rules may reduce status inequality and improve legal certainty.
Concurrent List Entry 5 supplies the legislative field.
Equality and dignity expose discriminatory civil rules.

groups.heading: QUALIFICATIONS
items: Article 44 is non-justiciable.
Uniformity may conceal majoritarian design if consultation is weak.
Religious freedom, culture, transition and federal diversity matter.

groups.heading: REFORM ROUTES
items: Target discriminatory rules first.
Use optional secular routes or harmonised principles where suitable.
A comprehensive code needs competence, consultation and safeguards.

stages.mechanism_strip: Uttarakhand: 2024 Act commenced 27 January 2025; the January 2026 Ordinance was succeeded by the Amendment Act published on 7 April 2026.
stages.answer_line: Article 44 supplies direction, while equality, pluralism, federal competence, consultation and transition determine whether a legislative design is constitutionally legitimate.

stages.title: PYQ ROUTES, PRELIMS TRAPS AND EXAM CONTROL

groups.heading: PRELIMS CONTROL
items: 36: State meaning; 37: duty without direct enforcement.
39(b) resources differs from 39(c) concentration.
41 has capacity limit; 45 is below six; 50 is a DPSP.

groups.heading: PYQ / EVIDENCE ROUTES
items: 2020: Article 50, UDHR, legal aid, welfare State and Part IV force.
2021: concentration; 2023 GS-II: NALSA.
2025 Part-matching key is locally official and verified.

groups.heading: MAINS ANSWER LADDER
items: Define through Articles 36-37.
Map exact Article, case and implementation mechanism.
Add federal, fiscal and institutional qualification.
Conclude with distributive ends through rights-disciplined means.

stages.mechanism_strip: A high-scoring answer moves from Article text to doctrine, implementation evidence, limits and a harmony-based conclusion.
stages.answer_line: PYQ control begins with the exact year, paper, wording and key status, then links the tested rule to its constitutional location.

stages.title: CURRENT-LAW AND EVIDENCE CONTROL
sequence: Check official Constitution, judgment or Gazette
State exact date and legal effect
Separate fact from inference and unresolved litigation
matrix: Suhas Chakma monitoring strengthens prison delivery
April 2026 Amendment Act succeeds January Ordinance

groups.heading: PRIMARY CONTROLS
items: Official Constitution text controls Articles 36-51.
Official Supreme Court judgments control Article 31C and legal-aid doctrine.
Official Gazette/government portal controls commencement and amendment status.

groups.heading: DO NOT OVERSTATE
items: Do not convert observations into a judicial command for UCC.
Do not treat every private asset as Article 39(b) material resource.
Do not cite volatile office holders as durable doctrine.

groups.heading: EXAM USE
items: Date every current status.
Name the instrument and legal effect.
Attach current evidence to the exact constitutional mechanism.

stages.mechanism_strip: Current affairs earn marks only when the source, date, instrument and constitutional relevance are all controlled.
stages.answer_line: Current evidence should prove implementation or legal status; it must never replace the exact constitutional rule.

stages.title: EXECUTABLE 10, 15 AND 20-MARK ANSWER ROUTES

groups.heading: 10 MARKS / 150 WORDS
items: Define through exact Article text.
Use three demand-specific points and one qualification.
Finish with a one-sentence direct verdict.

groups.heading: 15 MARKS / 250 WORDS
items: Use a chronology, comparison table or institutional chain.
Add current evidence and two diagnosed gaps.
Give reforms tied to those gaps.

groups.heading: 20 MARKS / 300 WORDS
items: Organise dimensions, not a catalogue of Articles.
Test law, institution, finance, delivery and rights limits.
Conclude substantial/partial/limited with reasons.

stages.mechanism_strip: Scale analytical dimensions and evidence with marks; do not merely lengthen the same generic answer.
stages.answer_line: A marks-worthy DPSP answer moves from exact text to mechanism, evidence, limitation and a demand-specific degree verdict.

stages.title: OPTIONAL ENRICHMENT: POSITIVE CONSTITUTIONALISM

groups.heading: ENRICHMENT LENSES
items: Positive constitutionalism requires public action as well as restraint.
Distributive review asks whether law genuinely advances common-good purposes.

groups.heading: USE WITH DISCIPLINE
items: Institutional competence limits judicial substitution.
Federal pluralism affects sequencing, finance and implementation.
Use only after the complete core answer is secure.
